subject: Two questions relating to latent growth model.

messages.author: d8517e92c7758dc2
messages.subject: Two questions relating to latent growth model.
parts:
Hi Professors, 

Here is Xueying again, and I feel sorry to bother you too much. 

Here I have two questions relating to latent growth model, the first question is about the time-invariant covariate in the latent growth model, and the second question is about piecewise latent growth model. 

The first question is listed below:   
I have been confused with the syntax in latent growth model when adding covariates. For example, there is a simple growth model below, and when there is no time-invariant covariates in the model, the growth model would be written like this: 

intercept=~1*x1+1*x2+1*x3+1*x4+1*x5 
slope=~0*x1+1*x2+2*x3+3*x4+4*x5 
intercept~1    # mean structure in lavaan 
slope~1          # mean structure in lavaan

But when adding the time-invariant covariates, I have seen two forms of syntax on the website, one form is: 
intercept=~1*x1+1*x2+1*x3+1*x4+1*x5 
slope=~0*x1+1*x2+2*x3+3*x4+4*x5 
intercept~covariate
slope~covariate

the other form is: 
intercept=~1*x1+1*x2+1*x3+1*x4+1*x5 
slope=~0*x1+1*x2+2*x3+3*x4+4*x5 
intercept~1+covariate 
slope~1+covariate

I would like to ask 1) if the two forms (the syntax marked in red) are both correct or not, 2) if so, what is the difference between them, 3) when to involve 1 (mean structure) into the syntax. 

The second question is listed as below: 
I would like to fit a piecewise latent growth model with the treatment variable in my data, where I would like to fit different latent growth models before and after the treatment was implemented into participants. however, the time-points when treatment was implemented was different in different persons, for example, some people were treated at the third time point, some were treated at the fourth time point. I know how to fit a piecewise latent growth model of the same knot, but have no idea how to fit the model of different knots even after I have read this paper "https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/pdf/10.1177/0013164413496812". Could you please give me any further suggestions or examples I could follow? 

Thank you very much. 

Regards 

Xueying

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Two questions relating to latent growth model.
parts: I would like to ask 1) if the two forms (the syntax marked in red) are both correct or not, 2) if so, what is the difference between them, 3) when to involve 1 (mean structure) into the syntax.

You want to estimate the means of the growth factors, unless you have some reason to fix the average initial-status or average rate-of-change to zero.  Regressing on the constant (intercept + slope ~ 1) frees their means in the syntax, or you could also simply use the lavaan() argument int.lv.free=TRUE to do so automatically (see the ?lavOptions help page), which is what the growth() wrapper does automatically.  That is probably why you have seen syntax with and without explicit latent means.

I know how to fit a piecewise latent growth model of the same knot, but have no idea how to fit the model of different knots even after I have read this paper "https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/pdf/10.1177/0013164413496812". Could you please give me any further suggestions or examples I could follow?

I am guessing that paper implemented it in Mplus, using the TSCORES option, which allows each subject to have different fixed loadings.  That is essentially how you allow for different knots per person, and it is also possible using "Definition variables" in OpenMx, but not possible in lavaan because everyone needs to have the same Lambda matrix.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.author: 12fdd832cacb825e
messages.subject: Re: Two questions relating to latent growth model.
parts:
An alternative for the piecewise qustion is to re-arrange every
participant's data so that the knot is at "time zero" for everyone.

For example, for respondents with the intervention at time 3,

tminus3 <- NA_real_
tminus2 <- x1
tminus1 <- x2
tzero <- x3
tplus1 <- x4
tplus2 <- x5

And for respondents with the intervention at time 4

tminus3 <- x1
tminus2 <- x2
tminus1 <- x3
tzero <- x4
tplus1 <- x5
tplus2 <- NA_real_

then

intercept =~ 1*tminus3 + 1*tminus2 + 1*tminus1 + 1*tzero + 1*tplus1 + 1*tplus2
preslope =~ -3*tminus3 -2*tminus2 -1*timinus1 + 0*tzero + 0*tplus1 + 0*tplus2
postslope =~ 0*timus3 + 0*tminus2 + 0*tminus1 + o 0*tzero + 1*tplus1 +1*tplus2

Of course, the 0* terms can be omitted--I just put them there for clarity.

This requires the assumption of no cohort interactions, but will let
you have the knot at different places.

Pat

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Two questions relating to latent growth model.
parts: if I use lavaan without argument int.lv.free=TRUE, the syntax should be "intercept+slope ~ 1+ covariate", but if I use growth() or lavaan() with this argument, the syntax should be "intercept + slope ~ covariate", am I correct?

Yes, although you can still include ~1 in the syntax anyway.  Explicit syntax should always override any defaults set with arguments (if there is an example that violates that principle, it is probably a bug).

Thanks for the creative solution, Pat!

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam

This requires the assumption of no cohort interactions, but will let
you have the knot at different places.

Just to clarify:
Pat's solution also assumes everyone has the same lag between observations before and after the knot, just like standard LGC models assume equal time intervals.  I only mention this because in my previous post, I mentioned each subject being able to have their own schedule using TSCORES or definition variables, and wanted to make sure you didn't continue to expect that using Pat's solution.

parts:
Hi Professors, 

This is Xueying again. I have a few more questions relating to the piecewise growth model which I have posted in the group several months ago. 

I draw a figure to illustrate my study design, briefly, as I have posted before, I would like to fit a piecewise growth model to assess whether the trajectory of Y variable would be different before and after certain intervention. The population in my study have repeated measurements of Y at six time points (T1-T6), and the data has the three features which might be considered when fitting piecewise model. First, the time-interval among follow-up time points were not exact the same for the adjacent time points, for example, the time-interval for T1 and T2 is 2 years apart, T2-T3 is 1 year apart, T3-T4 is 2 years apart, et al. (shown in Figure). Second, individuals had different numbers of repeated measurements of Y, for example, individual A had Y measurements at T1, T2 and T5, individual B had Y measurements at T3, T4 and T6, et al. Thirdly, individuals might have different intervention starting time points, for example, individual A started the intervention at T1, and individual B started the intervention at T3, however, majority of the population started the intervention at T3/T4.  




I followed the suggestions from previous post (smart idea from Patrick) to fit the piecewise growth model, that is, re-arranging every individual's data, and set the knot (the starting time point of the intervention) at "time zero" for everyone in the study. Therefore, I defined time-zero, time-minus*, time-plus* which were shown in the table below for different scenarios in which individuals had different time point of starting intervention (knot), and I also have considered the different time-intervals when defining time-minus* and time-plus*.  



I used the syntax like this to fit the piecewise growth model: 

intercept=~1*tminus7+1*tminus6+1*tminus5+1*tminus4+1*tminus3+1*tminus2+1*tminus0+1*tzero+1*tplus1+1*tplus2+1*tplus3+1*tplus4+1*tplus5+1*tplus6+1*tplus7
preslp=~(-7)*tminus7+(-6)*tminus6+(-5)*tminus5+(-4)*tminus4+(-3)*tminus3+(-2)*tminus2+(-1)*tminus0+0*tzero+0*tplus1+0*tplus2+0*tplus3+0*tplus4+0*tplus5+0*tplus6+0*tplus7
postslp=~0*tminus7+0*tminus6+0*tminus5+0*tminus4+0*tminus3+0*tminus2+0*tminus0+0*tzero+1*tplus1+2*tplus2+3*tplus3+4*tplus4+5*tplus5+6*tplus6+7*tplus7


So I have two questions for this piecewise model: 
1. As you have suggested before, this model assumed that ***everyone has the same lag between observations before and after the knot, just like standard LGC models assume equal time intervals***, I have tried to fit the model corresponding to the statement as much as possible (definition of time-zero, time-minus, and time-plus), but I still need your help to confirm whether I am doing the correct analysis. 

2. Currently, I used wave year as the time scale (figure above). Considering that age might be associated with Y and I adjusted baseline age (first measument of age as the covariate for latent intercept and slope), however, my colleagues have suggested that whether I could use biological age as the time scale in my analysis. So I would like to know first whether it's correct to use baseline age as covariate in my analysis. Then, I don't know whether it's reasonable to use age as time scale in this piecewise model. If so, I think age at the time point of starting intervention would be very heteregenous in different persons, and in this situation, shall I fit the piecewise growth model with random knot? Then how to fit a piecewise model with random knot? 

I have got lots of help from you and I appreciate you very much. 

Regards

Xueying
